lines: Middle Eastern crisis 2026 Iran war 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait Two Italian technicians working for Rheinmetall are killed and two other people are injured in a drone strike against a location in Kuwait. Iran has been blamed for the attack but denies responsibility. (BBC News)

Yemeni civil war Houthi–Saudi conflict Saudi Arabia says it has destroyed 50 Houthi military targets, including weapons depots, ballistic missile and drone launch sites, and command centres, in airstrikes on Sanaa, Al Hudaydah, and Saada Governorates in Yemen. (AA)

A clash between rival Bangladesh Nationalist Party factions in Munshiganj Sadar Upazila, Bangladesh, leaves one person dead and five injured by gunfire ahead of upcoming union parishad elections. (The Daily Star)

2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests Around 400 garment factories remain closed across Savar and Gazipur, Bangladesh, as workers rejected a newly announced ৳ 17,000 monthly minimum wage as insufficient block the Dhaka–Mymensingh and Dhaka–Tangail highways and clash with police firing tear gas and stun grenades. (The Business Standard)
Spanish economist Pablo Hernández de Cos is elected as the new president of the European Central Bank, succeeding French lawyer Christine Lagarde after her resignation. (Financial Times)

A business consortium led by U.S.-based asset management company Eldridge agrees to purchase international assets of Russian oil company Lukoil, including oil and gas fields, refineries, pipelines, and other infrastructure. (AP)
One crew member is killed and 16 more are rescued after the sinking of a Malta-flagged tanker off the coast of Ibiza, Spain. (Reuters)
At least nine people are injured, including three critically, in an explosion and fire at an Bangchak Corporation oil facility in Bangkok, Thailand. (AP)

2025 Cambridgeshire train stabbing The Cambridge Crown Court in the United Kingdom finds 32-year-old Anthony Williams guilty of the attempted murders of 14 people in three separate incidents, including the stabbing of ten people on a LNER train in November 2025. (AP)

2026 Giza fuel tanker explosion Egyptian prosecutors arrest a driver whose speeding car allegedly collided with a tank truck on Cairo's Ring Road yesterday, causing a fire that killed 31 people and injured 21 others. (AFP)
A shootout between minibus drivers after a quarrel on a street in Beirut, Lebanon, kills two people and injures three more. (L’Orient Today)
2026 Serbian presidential election The Serbian parliament sets the upcoming presidential election to December 27 after former president Aleksandar Vučić resigned in September. (AP)

Anti-corruption campaign under Xi Jinping At least 18 golf courses across China announce closures, including ten in Beijing, with many citing government orders following earlier restrictions on golf associated with paramount leader Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign. (AFP via France 24) (The Daily Telegraph)

Next Guinea-Bissau general election The Bissau-Guinean military government postpones presidential and legislative elections from December 2026 to November 2028, citing inadequate resources and logistical preparations, extending its transition to civilian rule following the November 2025 coup. (Reuters)

AI boom, Space policy of the United States The United States Federal Communications Commission authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites for its Starmind space-based data center network, despite concerns about space debris and interference with astronomical objects. (AFP)
